risk_if_not_implemented: Without Third-Party Exit Obligations Management, legal, regulatory, contractual, licensing and records-retention obligations tied to the relationship may lapse or be breached at cessation, creating liability the organization did not anticipate. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Contractual Default / Termination (R-EX-2), Regulatory / Legal / Contractual Financial Liability (R-EX-5), Uncontrolled Third-Party Security / Privacy Exposure (R-GV-5), Inability to Demonstrate Due Diligence / Due Care (R-GV-9), and most likely increases susceptibility to Dysfunctional Management Practices (MT-8), Human Error (MT-9), Statutory / Regulatory / Contractual Change (MT-11), Supplier Financial Distress / Insolvency (MT-24).

compensating_control_1.name: Third-Party Contract Requirements
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to require contractual requirements for applicable security, compliance and resilience requirements with third-parties, reflecting the organization's needs to protect its Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD).
compensating_control_1.justification: Third-Party Contract Requirements (TPM-14) compensates for the absence of Third-Party Exit Obligations Management (TPM-24.6) by specifying exit obligations in third-party contracts, which documents the commitments both parties must honor at termination. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Statutory, Regulatory & Contractual Compliance
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate the identification and implementation of relevant statutory, regulatory and contractual controls.
compensating_control_2.justification: Statutory, Regulatory & Contractual Compliance (CPL-02) compensates for the absence of Third-Party Exit Obligations Management (TPM-24.6) by identifying and implementing applicable statutory, regulatory and contractual controls, which captures the compliance obligations that survive or are triggered by a third-party exit. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
